# Slide 3: How it was (Data Ingestion) {background-color="#34495e"}

## Current version

Standard study folder structure — always in place. Within `datasets/`, versions accumulate:

-   `cohort_final.sas7bdat`
-   `cohort_final2.sas7bdat`
-   `cohort_final_USE_THIS.sas7bdat`

Version tracking: **filenaming + the OS modified date.**

. . .

**Naming is a social contract** — loosely enforced, inconsistent under pressure.

**Modified dates are fragile** — they reset silently on copy, sync, or backup.

. . .

::: {style="font-size: 1.4em; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
*Is this the right data? Has it changed?*
:::

# Slide 4: renv in practice {background-color="#34495e"}

## Current version

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**New project — run once**

```r
renv::init()       # isolated library + renv.lock
renv::upgrade()    # update renv itself

renv::install("ehrlinger/hvtiPlotR")
renv::install("tidyverse")

renv::snapshot()   # freeze versions
```

**Commit `renv.lock` — not the `renv/` folder.**
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Six months later — any analyst**

```r
# Open the .Rproj, then:
renv::restore()    # rebuild exact library
                   # from renv.lock
```

The lockfile is the recipe. `renv::restore()` rebuilds the library on any machine.
:::
::::::

## Design A — Timeline with lockfile as the handoff artifact

## Design B — Problem → Solution split

<style>
.split-panel {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 60px 1fr;
  gap: 0;

  height: 420px;
}

  padding: 6px 0;
  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.06);

}

  background: #1e1e1e;
  color: #ccc;

<div class="split-panel">
  <div class="panel-bad">
    <div class="panel-heading">Without renv</div>
    <div class="panel-item">📦 Packages installed globally — shared across all projects</div>
    <div class="panel-item">⚠️ <code>update.packages()</code> breaks other analyses silently</div>
    <div class="panel-item">⚠️ Serialized models in <code>estimates/</code> fail to load 6 months later</div>
    <div class="panel-item">❌ "Works on my machine" — but not yours</div>
    <div class="panel-item">❌ New analyst can't reproduce results without hunting down exact versions</div>
  </div>
  <div class="panel-divider">→</div>
  <div class="panel-good">
    <div class="panel-heading">With renv</div>
    <div class="panel-item">📦 Isolated library per project — updates don't bleed across</div>
    <div class="panel-item">✅ <code>renv.lock</code> records R version + every package version</div>
    <div class="panel-item">✅ <code>renv::restore()</code> rebuilds the exact library on any machine</div>
    <div class="panel-item">✅ The job belongs to the team, not the analyst</div>
    <div class="panel-code">
      renv::restore()<br>
      <span style="color:#6a9955;"># That's it. Same packages.</span><br>
      <span style="color:#6a9955;"># Same results.</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
